verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere documents an official CLI (Wally) that runs models from the terminal, locally and offline without an account, and one command 'points a tool at a model and starts it'. However, the evidence never explicitly describes an interactive text chat REPL; the session appears to come from launching an integrated tool such as opencode. Community hands-on reports of crashes concern the separate rcli voice demo, so they are not treated as a concrete contradiction here. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an interactive chat/REPL command, details of multi-turn session behavior in the terminal, independent hands-on corroboration of the Wally CLI chat flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start an interactive chat session with a model directly from the terminal

citations.quote: When a small model on your own machine is enough, the same CLI runs it, offline and without an account.
One command points a tool at a model and starts it. There is nothing to configure by hand
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
